content.comment_body: What is the difference between connecting a block or coil directly to the left rail versus connecting it through a 'high' contact?

Hello, There is essentially no difference. The block appears to be intended for use in function block diagrams and is not visible in ladder diagrams, except when converting from FBD to LAD. Regards, [user_name]

Hi, In my experience, creating programs in function block diagram is easier. If you're used to ladder diagrams it might seem simpler at first glance, but overall, FBD works better for me. I started with ladder diagrams as well, but switched to FBD fairly quickly and now stick with it. A major advantage is that everything is visually connected when linking one function block to another. In ladder diagrams, you need to carry the signal from one block to the next and then connect to a coil. When these elements are positioned differently, simulation, online testing, and troubleshooting become more complicated. Hope this helps.
I've never used function block diagrams before but have been interested in trying them. Your explanation is encouraging—thank you!

analysis.insight_summary: Users discuss the differences between ladder diagram and function block diagram programming methods in [company_name] PLC software. The consensus is that both approaches provide the same logical results, but FBD can simplify programming and make simulation, testing, and troubleshooting more visual and efficient compared to the more manual process in ladder diagrams when signals occur in various locations.
analysis.user_expectations: The user wants to understand the practical differences between using a 'high' contact versus a direct connection, and is interested in more straightforward and transparent programming techniques.
